text:
sara: Throwing an idea out — a client-assisted rollup for A/B canary detection and fallback. Clients emit tiny 'quality pings' and a lightweight coordinator aggregates to decide cutover. Local clients can short-circuit in extreme cases. Pros: fast localized fallback and distributed detection. Cons: noisy signals, security surface, complexity. Thoughts?

mike: are clients advisory only or can they force a local fallback?

sara: advisory by default. Flow: client -> vote to coordinator -> coordinator aggregates -> signed policy broadcast. But client may short-circuit to fallback variant temporarily until a coordinator policy arrives.

alex: that hybrid model needs clear interface boundaries: 1) vote schema, 2) signed coordinator policy with TTL+nonce, 3) audit trail.

jen: telemetry/security: scrub PII from votes, KMS-signed policies, rate limits on votes.

sara: draft vote payload (minimal):
```
{
  "client_id": "c-1234",
  "variant": "A",
  "window_s": 30,
  "latency_p90_ms": 320,
  "error_rate": 0.07,
  "semantic_score": 0.82
}
```
we'd hash session id and avoid free-text. coordinator signs responses.

mike: quorum selection? random sample vs reservoir per cohort. avoid thundering herd. per-tenant thresholds too.

alex: use weighted Bayesian math: each vote has weight w_i (client reliability). compute posterior P(quality < target). trigger when posterior exceeds threshold. reduces false positives from noisy clients.

jen: infra/ops: coordinator must be backpressure-resistant. stream-aggregate asynchronously into short-term reducer (approximate). bucket metrics to preserve privacy.

sara: policy issuance sketch (signed):
```
{
  "policy_id": "pol-2026-03-10-17",
  "action": "fallback",
  "target_variant": "B",
  "scope": {"cohort": "beta", "region": "us-east-1"},
  "ttl_s": 120,
  "signature": "kms-sig-v1",
  "reason": "weighted_posterior=0.93",
  "observed_metrics_ref": "s3://hashes/obs-434"
}
```
clients validate signature+scope+TTL and apply atomically.

mike: what if clients never hear coordinator? add soft-expiry and periodic pull reconcile. safe-mode: revert after TTL if no policy confirmation.

alex: add proof-of-observation tokens so coordinator can challenge stale clients for audits. require idempotency keys when applying policies.

jen: test matrix: coordinator partition chaos, malicious noisy clients, per-region noise, per-tenant isolation. measure time-to-cutover and recovery.

sara: success metrics: false-positive rate <1% per rollout, mean local short-circuit <10s, mean global policy enforcement <60s, audit completeness >=99%.

mike: who owns the coordinator? infra can prototype.

jen: i'll take telemetry+security (signing & privacy). will run gating experiments.

sara: i'll write RFC follow-up with interfaces and a minimal prototype plan: coordinator as small stateless aggregator + Redis short store. tagging @mike @jen @alex to sync.

ops-bot: scheduled: canary-protocol-experiment created (id: cpe-47) — staging cluster reserved.

deploy-bot: staging deploy for cpe-47 OK — smoke tests passed :white_check_mark:

mike: +1. keep initial rollout internal, ramp to beta after 48h stable telemetry.

sara: will include stepwise ramp and gating matrix in RFC. thanks all.
